correctness.rationale: A direct cyclic Bessel alias representation and factorial tail bound prove the flux-uniform t-step TV inequality, including both coherent and incoherent tail-square terms. The characteristic function J_0(4Jτ sin(ξ/2)) has unique modulus-one frequency 0 and quadratic expansion, yielding the circle heat kernel in total variation at t=floor(s n²). Strict heat-kernel contraction gives the no-cutoff conclusion. Odd-cycle directional probability coefficients vanish below girth n, with the first coefficient obtained from direct-versus-longest-short-path interference; even-cycle symmetry follows from bipartite sign conjugation. Verifier checks 702 finite parameter instances but does not replace proof.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a motivated boundary question arising from dephased gauge-flux quantum-walk spectral transitions: at fixed coherent interval, microscopic chirality is visible first at the odd girth but its macroscopic diffusive mixing profile and epsilon-mixing times are flux-independent uniformly in the flux. A quantitative factorial estimate makes the finite-size and time-scale tradeoff explicit, distinguishing complete position dephasing from local detection with different long-size scaling. This is an all-size structural law, not an isolated parameter evaluation.
